headline: Controversy: State Minister Ishraque Ahmed resigns after gun-in-hand drug drive
summary: The minister claimed he carried a firearm for security during the operation, but resigned to prevent party embarrassment.
details: State Minister Ishraque Ahmed has resigned from his position following a controversial 'drug drive' where he was seen carrying a firearm.
During a press conference at the National Press Club, Ishraque stated that he voluntarily sought to resign to avoid embarrassing his party and to focus on anti-drug efforts.
He defended his actions, claiming that the police were unequipped and that he carried the firearm for his own security during the anti-drug operation.
The Cabinet Division has received his resignation letter, and an official notification is expected to be issued shortly.
Meanwhile, a joint operation was conducted at the same spot where the initial drive took place, resulting in the arrest and sentencing of 15 people.
Critics, including Nahid Islam, have called on the government to provide a full explanation for the circumstances surrounding the resignation.
caption:
A State Minister resigns after being seen with a gun during a drug raid. He claims it was for security, but the party was embarrassed.

State Minister Ishraque Ahmed has resigned from his position following a controversial 'drug drive' where he was seen carrying a firearm.

During a press conference at the National Press Club, Ishraque stated that he voluntarily sought to resign to avoid embarrassing his party and to focus on anti-drug efforts.

He defended his actions, claiming that the police were unequipped and that he carried the firearm for his own security during the anti-drug operation.

The Cabinet Division has received his resignation letter, and an official notification is expected to be issued shortly.

Meanwhile, a joint operation was conducted at the same spot where the initial drive took place, resulting in the arrest and sentencing of 15 people.

Critics, including Nahid Islam, have called on the government to provide a full explanation for the circumstances surrounding the resignation.

#Bangladesh #Politics #IshraqueAhmed #Government #News

Source: bdnews24.com, Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV, Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star

headline_marked: Saudi Arabia [[executes two Bangladeshis]], Jamaat-e-Islami chief questions embassy role
headline: Saudi Arabia executes two Bangladeshis, Jamaat-e-Islami chief questions embassy role
summary: Opposition leader Dr. Shafiqur Rahman has called for government transparency regarding the legal assistance provided to the two citizens before their execution.
details: Two Bangladeshi citizens were recently executed in the holy city of Mecca, Saudi Arabia, sparking widespread discussion and criticism across various media and social platforms.
Dr. Shafiqur Rahman, the Amir of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami and Leader of the Opposition in the National Parliament, raised several questions on Facebook regarding the executions.

He emphasized that embassies and consulates are established to protect the interests and dignity of expatriates, questioning whether the Bangladesh embassy or consulate was involved in the judicial process of the two men.

The Jamaat chief pointed out that statements from government officials suggesting they only learned of the executions after the fact raise serious concerns about the state's role in protecting its citizens.
He urged the government to clarify to the public whether the embassy fulfilled its responsibilities in this death penalty case, as the individuals involved were Bangladeshi expatriates.
Dr. Rahman also called for the government to take initiatives to prevent future expatriates from being deprived of necessary legal assistance during judicial proceedings in foreign countries.
He stressed that it is the government's responsibility to ensure that expatriates are aware of the laws of the host country to avoid such tragic outcomes.
Finally, he suggested that instead of merely discussing the executions, all parties should review their positions to ensure better protection for Bangladeshi workers abroad.
caption:
Two Bangladeshis have been executed in Saudi Arabia. Now, the government is being questioned over whether its embassy provided necessary legal aid.

Two Bangladeshi citizens were recently executed in the holy city of Mecca, Saudi Arabia, sparking widespread discussion and criticism across various media and social platforms.

Dr. Shafiqur Rahman, the Amir of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami and Leader of the Opposition in the National Parliament, raised several questions on Facebook regarding the executions.

He emphasized that embassies and consulates are established to protect the interests and dignity of expatriates, questioning whether the Bangladesh embassy or consulate was involved in the judicial process of the two men.

The Jamaat chief pointed out that statements from government officials suggesting they only learned of the executions after the fact raise serious concerns about the state's role in protecting its citizens.

He urged the government to clarify to the public whether the embassy fulfilled its responsibilities in this death penalty case, as the individuals involved were Bangladeshi expatriates.

Dr. Rahman also called for the government to take initiatives to prevent future expatriates from being deprived of necessary legal assistance during judicial proceedings in foreign countries.

He stressed that it is the government's responsibility to ensure that expatriates are aware of the laws of the host country to avoid such tragic outcomes.

Finally, he suggested that instead of merely discussing the executions, all parties should review their positions to ensure better protection for Bangladeshi workers abroad.
